text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- GOVT STIMULATES EXPORTS
Economists and exporters welcomed the government's recently announced measures to stimulate exports, saying steps to pre-finance exports were most efficient in boosting the sector.
-- BANKS EARN 51 PERCENT MORE ON SERVICE CHARGES

A survey shows banks have increased their receipts from service charges by 51 percent in the first nine months of this year compared with the same period last year. This figure does not yet include the full effect of the freeing up of bank charges in July this year.
-- GOVT HELPS STATE BANKS

The government is adopting a series of measures to facilitate the privatization of state banks and can now act as a guarantor for credits given to states who are reforming their banks and cleaning up their books.
O GLOBO
-- CAPITAL ENTERING BRAZIL IMPROVES

The amount of short term speculative capital entering Brazil has fallen to $4.3 billion between January and September this year from $16.5 billion in the same period last year, while direct investment has grown to $8 billion.
-- MINISTER THREATENS NOT TO ADHERE TO REDUNDANCY PROGRAM
Social Security Minister Reinhold Stephanes threatened not to adhere to the government's voluntary redundancy program, saying he could not accept job cuts in certain areas of his department.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- LANDLESS DECIDE TO INVADE MORE ESTATES
The landless peasant movement decided its main strategy to promote agrarian reform in 1997 would be the invasion of landed estates.
-- AVIATION DEATHS HIT RECORD IN 1996
In 1996, 177 people died in 82 aviation accidents in Brazil, the highest number of deaths in the last 14 years and fifth highest of all times, according to government figures.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
